comparison: Perfect agreement on reporter system validation (C43-C92). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with strong praise. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary approaches and expected responses to modulators, while peer reviewers describe the system as 'elegant' and 'reliable.'

Strong agreement on CRISPR screen and SFSWAP identification (C5, C46-C54, C93-C94). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights orthogonal validation methods and timing data, while peer reviewers praise the screen as 'elegant,' 'state-of-the-art,' and 'convincing.' Peer review also includes C40 which OpenEval addresses separately in R3.

OpenEval R3 addresses RT-qPCR validation of OGT splicing changes (C40, C53, C54) as SUPPORTED. These claims overlap with peer R2's broader evaluation of the CRISPR screen and validation experiments, which also finds the evidence SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluations of global RNA-seq analysis (C6, C55-C60). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED despite noting limited functional enrichment. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about controls and off-target effects from siRNA treatment, though revision comments suggest concerns were addressed.

Perfect agreement on decoy exon mechanism for OGT (C7, C41, C61-C65). Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes complementary approaches and appropriate use of UPF1 knockdown, while peer reviewers find the decoy mechanism data 'compelling' with no specific criticisms.

Divergent evaluations of global decoy exon analysis (C8, C42, C67-C70). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to complex bidirectional results and potential false positives in computational predictions. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, finding the model 'intriguing' and praising the 'sophisticated bioinformatic analysis' without specific criticism.

Agreement on mechanistic insights regarding SF1 and SRSF1 (C77-C79). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with prior in vitro studies, while peer reviewers accept the current mechanistic detail and acknowledge room for future exploration.

Divergent evaluations of O-GlcNAc-SFSWAP mechanistic link (C80-C81). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on cited phosphoproteomics data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'No firm evidence linking SFSWA to an O-GlcNAc specific mechanism,' though not considered a major limitation.

Agreement on limitations of SFSWAP's role (C82). Both find this SUPPORTED as an acknowledged limitation. OpenEval notes importance for understanding additional regulatory factors, while peer reviewers accept the incomplete mechanistic understanding with appropriate speculation.

OpenEval R10 evaluates background claims on decoy exon function from prior literature (C71-C76) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not separately assess background/contextual claims.

OpenEval R11 evaluates extensive background and contextual claims (C1-C4, C9-C39, C58, C66) as SUPPORTED based on prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on novel experimental findings rather than background claims.
